questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study Spanish, so Spain made sense to improve my language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there is a meeting with the Erasmus office, and they send you a lot of info e-mails as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't need any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy with the website Idealista. You can draw a map, and they send you relevant appartments within that zone.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The campus is in the north, so don't choose a place too much in the south. Madrid is a big city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you have two weeks to try classes, before regisering officially. You get all info you need on e-mail, and they also explain everything to you at the intro-meeting, so it was very easy. in the faculty of filology you need to have a C1 level of Spanish, and all info is in Spanish.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus office was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the 2 weeks trial. I thought I knew which classes I wanted, but after I tried one, I decided to change for another.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is high, especially language wise. In facultad de filología you are expected to speak and understand Spanish at a high level upon arrival, and even then it was hard to follow sometimes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different. More high school like, with more exercises, and your are expected to participate and get evaluated on that in your grade. You are also expected to be physically present in most classes, which is different from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Heterogeneidad cultural y mestizaje
- Crisis del realismo y fundadores de la nueva narrativa
- Poesía de la postvanguardia y poetas contemporáneos

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: - Crisis del realismo y fundadores de la nueva narrativa. Bethania is a great professor, and her class is very interesting. In general the community on the master Literatura Hispanoamericana is very sociable which is great as an exchange student.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The heating bill was very high as many buildings in Madrid are old and not insulated. But even included, in total my rent did not cross 5000 dkk

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is cheaper that Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Music, dance, sports, choir, volunteer work.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I took dance lessons off campus, and met a lot of great local people that way.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: the villages north of Madrid like El Escorial, Segovia etc. You can take a bus or rent a car very cheap, and it takes no time to be in nature, mountains and beautiful small villages. Great sunday plan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Spanyards are great people but speak very fast, interrupt a lot, and they don't slow down to include you in the conversation. So it was a bit tough in the beginning to feel included, but I believe I adapted quickly to the new circumstances.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Master in Literatura Hispanoamericana. If you study Spanish, take all of your courses the same place, so you see the same people in each class. It is worth it to get to know someone outside the Erasmus circle while yout here. You also have to actively look for it, and take initiative although it can be tough. It will be worth it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Spanyards can be extremely direct and interrupt a lot. It can come across as rude for a dane, but it's really just a cultural difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way everything is centered around being out in the city and socializing a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Look for friendships in local communities. It is worth is.
Don't be afraid to try again when you fail. You are here to learn, and in the end you will realize how far you've come. 
Don't worry that you feel shy or don't understand everything. Your energy, personality and abilities come across more than you think.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Madrid is an amazing city, and I don't think anyone will regret going there. It is colder in the winter than you might think though, so bring warm clothes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the amazing people I befriended.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Getting on the level of Spanish where I didn't feel lost in conversations ever.  
Understanding my Andaluz professor.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
